messages:
maria: quick heads-up — staging perf regression on llama2-13b-q4f16 when batch size >=8. tail latency jumps ~20% and some requests see 50–120ms extra. attached perfetto/nsys.

maria: repro: synthetic Poisson arrivals ~30qps, seq len mix 64/256/512, warm kvcache then ramp. observed kernel variant switch around t=2.1s.

tom: can you share the traces/links? did kernel selection flip to the fallback kernel? nvprof/nsys graphs pls.

maria: perfetto: https://perfetto.app/trace/xyz-quant-handoff (short link). nsys snapshot: 
- high-level: GPU time stable, but host queue time spikes during handoff
- kernel switch: fast_q_matmul -> matmul_generic at 02.1s
- kvcache hit-rate drops from 0.99 -> 0.85 at the same time

maria: nvprof snippet (abridged):
```
# nvprof --analysis-metrics ...
Kernel: fast_q_matmul Launch 12ms compute 1.8ms
Kernel: matmul_generic Launch 14ms compute 3.6ms
Host gap between kernel launches ~1.6ms (extra)
```

anil: that looks like a kernel handoff cost (launch/ptx path). continuous batching window is 20ms by default — fragments can push mixed shapes into the same window and we choose a conservative generic matmul.

lucy: also saw cudaEvent elapsed between kernels increase; suspect small JIT/PTX link or different kernel config path for quantized variant leading to GPU-side kernel rebind.

trace-bot: automated analysis: probable causes: (1) variant selection flip due to batch content change, (2) kvcache eviction causing longer KV restore, (3) host scheduling gap triggering kernel reconfiguration. Estimated extra latency ~1.2–2.4ms per affected request.

maria: quick workaround idea: (A) increase continuous_batching.window_ms from 20 -> 50 to reduce fragmentation, (B) add heuristic to prefer keeping current kernel variant for next N windows if switching cost > expected benefit, (C) bias kernel selection using recent seq distribution and kvhit probability.

tom: I'll run an A/B with window_ms=50 and window_ms=100 and capture nsys. also will try a 'sticky kernel' flag in the batcher to test.

anil: proposal for selection cost model:
- measure cost_switch = avg_host_gap + avg_kernel_setup_overhead
- estimate benefit = delta_compute_time * expected_batch_token_count
- if benefit < cost_switch * safety_factor, avoid switching

lucy: added trace tags in the new trace build: kernel.variant, kvcache.evicted, batching.window_ms. re-running traces now.

maria: thanks. action items: tom (run perf runs with 50/100ms and sticky flag, post nsys & perfetto), anil (proto cost-model in batcher, test in local sim), lucy (collect traces and images), i'll open an issue and link traces.

tom: ack :thumbsup:

maria: GH issue opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/issues/4212 - includes summary + trace links + initial screenshots.

lucy: attaching small perfetto screenshot (uploaded) — shows queue spike aligned with kernel switch.

anil: if sticky heuristic ok, we can also incorporate kv cache signals (if kv hit rate falls < threshold, prevent switch) — keeps prefix locality.

maria: agreed. also watch for regressions on dedicated. let's run smoke on a dedicated box after changes.

tom: will do smoke + perf on dedicated once experiments finish.

maria: thanks team — let's sync in tomorrow eng-runtime stand if we have results.
